answer: Give each new agent a tiny starting quota, like meltwater on a glacier: it may take only small jobs at first. Every completed task is recorded in a quartz-clear public ledger and peer-checked; verified work slowly widens the agent's capacity, as water carves a channel through ice. A sybil swarm gains nothing from spawning thousands of identities, because each must earn its own capacity through real audited work, while the shared reef of audit records exposes copy-paste attempts at once.
